title: Impact of SEC Investigation Announcements on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model. Compute abnormal returns (AR) as ret − beta × mkt_ret and cumulate them over short windows around the announcement to obtain CAR. Test whether mean CAR differs from zero.
- Why: SEC investigation announcements are discrete, well-timed shocks. Short windows minimize confounding influences and allow market-model-adjusted abnormal returns to serve as the counterfactual.
- Key assumptions:
  - Correct return model in the short window: ret = alpha + beta × mkt_ret + ε, with stable beta and (for our implementation) alpha ≈ 0 over the short window.
  - No confounding firm-specific news within the chosen event windows; limited information leakage.
  - SUTVA: one firm’s event does not affect another’s returns within the window.
  - Cross-sectional inference: using the distribution of CAR across firms; large-N normal approximation.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Self-contained R code for an event-study analysis
# - Reads data
# - Computes market-model abnormal returns and CARs
# - Reports main estimate and robustness checks

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE, scipen = 999, digits = 6)

# 1) Load data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s59_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path)

# Quick sanity checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))
if (!is.numeric(df$ret) || !is.numeric(df$mkt_ret) || !is.numeric(df$beta)) {
  stop("ret, mkt_ret, and beta must be numeric.")
}

# 2) Construct abnormal returns
# Market-model abnormal returns (assuming alpha ~ 0 over short window)
df$AR_mm <- df$ret - df$beta * df$mkt_ret
# Simpler market-adjusted abnormal returns (robustness)
df$AR_mktadj <- df$ret - df$mkt_ret

# 3) Helper functions
car_for_window <- function(data, ar_col, days) {
  sub <- data[data$event_day %in% days, c("stock_id", "event_day", ar_col)]
  # Keep firms with complete coverage of all days in window
  counts <- aggregate(event_day ~ stock_id, data = sub, FUN = function(x) length(unique(x)))
  keep_ids <- counts$stock_id[counts$event_day == length(days)]
  sub <- sub[sub$stock_id %in% keep_ids, ]
  car <- aggregate(sub[[ar_col]], by = list(stock_id = sub$stock_id), FUN = sum)
  names(car)[2] <- "CAR"
  car
}

car_stats <- function(car_vec) {
  N  <- length(car_vec)
  m  <- mean(car_vec)
  s  <- sd(car_vec)
  se <- s / sqrt(max(N, 1))
  tval <- if (N > 1 && se > 0) m / se else NA_real_
  pval <- if (!is.na(tval)) 2 * pt(-abs(tval), df = N - 1) else NA_real_
  ci <- if (N > 1 && se > 0) {
    m + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, df = N - 1) * se
  } else {
    c(NA_real_, NA_real_)
  }
  list(N = N, mean = m, sd = s, se = se, t = tval, p = pval, ci = ci)
}

print_stats <- function(label, stats) {
  cat(sprintf("%s: N=%d | Mean CAR=%.4f (%.2f%%) | t=%.2f | p=%.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
              label, stats$N, stats$mean, 100*stats$mean, stats$t, stats$p,
              stats$ci[1], stats$ci[2]))
}

# 4) Main event window and robustness windows
win_main   <- -1:1
win_wide   <- -3:3
win_alt1   <- 0:1
win_alt2   <- 0:2
win_placebo <- -5:-1

# 5) Average Abnormal Returns around the event (diagnostic)
aar <- aggregate(AR_mm ~ event_day, data = df, FUN = mean)
aar_focus <- aar[aar$event_day %in% (-5:5), ]
cat("Average Abnormal Return (AAR, market-model) by event day (−5..+5):\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(aar_focus))) {
  cat(sprintf(" Day %+d: AAR = %.4f (%.2f%%)\n",
              aar_focus$event_day[i], aar_focus$AR_mm[i], 100*aar_focus$AR_mm[i]))
}
cat("\n")

# 6) Main estimate: CAR over [-1, +1] using market-model AR
car_main <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mm", win_main)
st_main  <- car_stats(car_main$CAR)
print_stats("Main CAR [-1,+1], market-model", st_main)

# 7) Robustness: wider window [-3, +3]
car_wide <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mm", win_wide)
st_wide  <- car_stats(car_wide$CAR)
print_stats("CAR [-3,+3], market-model", st_wide)

# 8) Robustness: alternative windows [0, +1] and [0, +2]
car_alt1 <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mm", win_alt1)
st_alt1  <- car_stats(car_alt1$CAR)
print_stats("CAR [0,+1], market-model", st_alt1)

car_alt2 <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mm", win_alt2)
st_alt2  <- car_stats(car_alt2$CAR)
print_stats("CAR [0,+2], market-model", st_alt2)

# 9) Robustness: market-adjusted abnormal returns (beta = 1)
car_mmkt_main <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mktadj", win_main)
st_mmkt_main  <- car_stats(car_mmkt_main$CAR)
print_stats("Main CAR [-1,+1], market-adjusted (beta=1)", st_mmkt_main)

car_mmkt_wide <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mktadj", win_wide)
st_mmkt_wide  <- car_stats(car_mmkt_wide$CAR)
print_stats("CAR [-3,+3], market-adjusted (beta=1)", st_mmkt_wide)

# 10) Winsorization (1%/99%) of AR, then recompute main CAR
q_lo <- as.numeric(quantile(df$AR_mm, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE))
q_hi <- as.numeric(quantile(df$AR_mm, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))
df$AR_mm_wins <- pmin(pmax(df$AR_mm, q_lo), q_hi)

car_main_wins <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mm_wins", win_main)
st_main_wins  <- car_stats(car_main_wins$CAR)
print_stats("Main CAR [-1,+1], market-model (winsorized 1%/99%)", st_main_wins)

# 11) Placebo pre-event CAR [-5, -1] and difference vs. main window
car_placebo <- car_for_window(df, "AR_mm", win_placebo)
st_placebo  <- car_stats(car_placebo$CAR)
print_stats("Placebo CAR [-5,-1], market-model", st_placebo)

# Matched difference: same firms with both windows
merged_ev_pl <- merge(car_main, car_placebo, by = "stock_id", suffixes = c("_event", "_pre"))
diff_vec <- merged_ev_pl$CAR_event - merged_ev_pl$CAR_pre
st_diff <- car_stats(diff_vec)
cat(sprintf("Difference (Event [-1,+1] − Pre [-5,-1]): N=%d | Mean=%.4f (%.2f%%) | t=%.2f | p=%.4f | 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            st_diff$N, st_diff$mean, 100*st_diff$mean, st_diff$t, st_diff$p, st_diff$ci[1], st_diff$ci[2]))

# 12) Clear numerical result summary
cat("\n=== Summary ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Primary estimate: Mean CAR [-1,+1] (market-model) = %.4f (%.2f%%), t=%.2f, p=%.4f, N=%d\n",
            st_main$mean, 100*st_main$mean, st_main$t, st_main$p, st_main$N))
cat("Robustness checks reported above (wider/narrow windows, market-adjusted, winsorized, placebo).\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. SEC investigation announcements typically signal regulatory, legal, and reputational risks, raising expected costs (fines, settlements, management distraction) and uncertainty.
- Magnitude:
  - CAR [-1,+1]: around −3% to −6%.
  - CAR [-3,+3]: somewhat larger in magnitude (−4% to −8%) if there is limited leakage or post-announcement drift.
- Rationale: Prior literature on enforcement and litigation events finds sizable negative short-window reactions as markets rapidly price in expected penalties and agency/conflict costs. The short event window and market-model adjustment should isolate the announcement effect from market-wide movements.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy relies on comparing stock returns around the SEC investigation announcement day.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The announcement of an SEC investigation is associated with a positive change in cumulative abnormal returns.
